clue.text: Married couple and lieutenant cuddling is stuff of fantasy

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap your arms round something, so each pair of outer letters holds the next word inside

parts.note: a married couple is a wife and husband, W and H
taken as written, held by the couple
LT is the standard abbreviation for lieutenant
the same word does double duty, held by the officer too

explanation.surface: A couple and an army officer snuggling up is the material of daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddling is' applies to both subjects at once, so the one small word is used twice; W and H are the standard abbreviations for wife and husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list is a set of hoped-for things, the material of daydreams and fantasy.

clue.text: Somewhere to hang hospital gown?

parts.note: a ward is a room in a hospital
a robe is a long gown

explanation.surface: A question about where you would hang up a hospital gown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of a gown to hang; 'Somewhere to hang' is the definition and 'hospital gown' builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a cupboard where clothes are hung up on rails.

clue.text: Suspend outrageous parodies

indicators.note: something outrageous is wildly out of order, so the letters of the word before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to halt parodies that have gone too far.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-up is a mocking imitation, the same thing as a parody or spoof.

clue.text: See 21 down

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see! or behold!
21 is the answer to 21 down, weight, and W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: An ordinary cross-reference telling the solver to look at another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a pointer to a linked clue, but every word works: the instruction itself is the wordplay and 'down' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low and feeling down both mean being sad or dejected, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Stomach is churning with sodas — they make it sore

indicators.note: churning stirs and mixes things, so the letters of the words around it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fizzy drinks upset the stomach and leave it aching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they make it sore' seems to describe the sodas, but it is a playful definition: these people enjoy giving and receiving pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadomasochists take pleasure in inflicting and suffering pain, so they deliberately cause soreness.

clue.text: Plants beginning to cause rash

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of cause
hives is an itchy skin rash

explanation.surface: Some plants start off a skin rash when touched.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are small onion-family herbs, grown as garden plants.

clue.text: Labour target regenerating after cuts at the top

definitions.text: Labour target regenerating after cuts at the top

parts.note: surface reading: an aim of the Labour Party, renewing itself after cuts by senior figures

parts.words: regenerating after cuts at the top
parts.note: setter's reading: the beast slain in one of Hercules' twelve Labours, which grew back a head each time one was cut off

explanation.surface: A political party's goal recovering after its leadership is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks political but means one of the twelve Labours of Hercules; his second was to kill a many-headed serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lernaean serpent regrew two heads for every one Hercules severed, until the stumps were burned.

clue.text: I got drunk after very briefly feeling high

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word just before loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about out of order, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy who briefly feels light-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the jumbled letters behind the shortened word, so read the clue's second half first.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a dizzy, spinning sensation, especially a fear of heights, which is a feeling when high up.

clue.text: Band run out of clothes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stripe or line of colour
second meaning: to dash naked through a public place

explanation.walkthrough: 'run out of clothes' sounds like having nothing left to wear; it means running with none on.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a narrow stripe; as a verb it means dashing about naked in public.

clue.text: Solver's wrong about end of puzzle? Count last words

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you, so what belongs to the solver is yours
a sin is a wrong
C stands for circa, about

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the last letter of puzzle
to count on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A setter teases the solver over getting the final answer wrong and ending up with a count.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the clue in two, but it is one long charade; 'last words' means the sign-off at the foot of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours sincerely is the customary closing phrase of a formal letter, the final words before the signature.

clue.text: Frenchman joined a union that's modernised

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
to wed is to join in the union of marriage

explanation.surface: A Frenchman signs up to a trade union that has been updated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but here it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something renewed has been restored or brought up to date, made fresh and modern again.

clue.text: One directs former racketeer to replace iron with gold

indicators.note: to replace one thing with another means swapping one set of letters out for a different set

parts.note: Roger Federer, the retired tennis champion, wielded a racket
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A mob boss gets someone to swap iron for gold, as if running an alchemy scam.
explanation.walkthrough: A racketeer is usually a gangster; here it is a racket player, the tennis star Federer, whose opening FE becomes OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderer is someone who gives orders or commands, that is, one who directs others.

clue.text: Trump caught in a bad lie, perhaps

definitions.note: golf: a ball in the long grass sits badly

indicators.note: caught here means caught by the ear, heard rather than seen written

parts.note: to ruff is to play a trump card in bridge or whist

explanation.surface: Donald Trump, a keen golfer, is caught out telling a nasty untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' and 'lie' point at politics; the clue is really about cards and golf, where a ball's lie is how it sits on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the rough is the long grass off the fairway, where a ball has a poor lie.

clue.text: Swinger is one moaning, naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outermost letters are taken away

parts.note: a whinger is someone who complains or moans

explanation.surface: A sexually adventurous person is found moaning in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a partner-swapper; it is simply something that swings, like a door on its fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the joint on which a door or lid swings open and shut.

clue.text: Cocktail at marriage, endless supply!

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bendily, so the letters are flexed into a new order
endless means without an ending, so the last letter of the preceding word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A wedding bar where the cocktails never run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun for stocks of drink, but it is read as supple-ly, an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila cocktail with lime and orange liqueur, served in a salt-rimmed glass.

clue.text: Where to study bulls and bears, ferrets and fish

definitions.text: Where to study bulls and bears

parts.note: a business is the collective noun for a group of ferrets
a school is the collective noun for a group of fish

explanation.surface: A zoology course covering bulls, bears, ferrets and fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The animals all look like one zoo list, but bulls and bears are stock-market traders who expect rises and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A business school teaches finance and management, including how bullish and bearish markets behave.

clue.text: Lines of dialogue between human and pigeon recorded

indicators.note: a recording is something listened to, so the sounds matter rather than the spelling

parts.note: a person greets with hi and a pigeon answers with its coo

explanation.surface: Someone tapes a chat between a person and a pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines, so it is a set of verse lines.

clue.text: Parks in reverse without aim, like an idiot

indicators.note: in reverse means going backwards, so the word before is read from its end

parts.note: to park something somewhere is to put it there
doing something idly is doing it aimlessly

explanation.surface: A driver who reverses into a parking space without aiming, behaving foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting stupidly means behaving foolishly, in the manner of an idiot.

clue.text: Old piece of crust that's extremely dry

parts.note: super means very or extremely, as in super keen
continent is the opposite of incontinent: in control of the bladder, so staying dry

explanation.surface: A stale bit of pie or bread crust that has dried right out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crust' suggests baking, but it is the Earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercontinent such as Pangaea was an ancient landmass of the Earth's crust joining today's continents.

clue.text: Relative docked when heading to plane to prepare for takeoff

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of plane

explanation.surface: A relative whose plane has docked heads to another, getting ready for departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takeoff' suggests a plane, but it is taking off a bracelet or belt by first opening its fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclasp is to undo a fastening, the first step in removing a necklace or bag strap.

clue.text: Piece of work runs into bar

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: bar can mean except, as in 'all bar one'
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone who runs into a pub after a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer piece of writing or music, a section of a work.

clue.text: Brawn won over rowing team

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for won in sports tables
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Muscle power beat a rowing crew.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight here is heft or physical bulk and power, the same sense as brawn or muscle.

clue.text: Tiny label read out by setter's too much

indicators.note: reading something out says it aloud, so its sound gives the letters, not its spelling

parts.note: XS, extra small, is the clothing label for the tiniest size
the setter is I, so setter's here is short for I have

explanation.surface: A setter reading out a minuscule label is overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: XS on a clothes tag means extra small; said out loud it is the first part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive means more than is needed or reasonable, the same as too much.

clue.text: More than one nerd packs up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to stow is to pack away

explanation.surface: Several geeks pack their bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Swots are students who study too hard, a British word for nerds or bookworms.

clue.text: Sun's beginning to disappear? Better take top off!

indicators.note: when the beginning disappears, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: the word sun, which then loses its first letter
to cap a story is to better it

explanation.surface: As the sun sets, someone suggests removing a sunhat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like advice, 'you'd better'; it is the verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap something is to remove its lid or cap, as with a pen or bottle.

clue.text: Travel round state, fighting

parts.note: Goa is a state of India
a bout is a fight or boxing match

explanation.surface: A tour of a state where fighting is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: To go about can mean to move or travel around from place to place.

clue.text: Stop entertaining frightfully rude bore

indicators.note: frightfully means in a dreadful way, so the next word comes out in a mess
to entertain guests is to have them in your house, so one part is held inside another

parts.note: to end is to stop
the word rude, jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stops hosting a dreadfully rude and tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a noun, a dull person, but it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Endured and bore are both past tenses meaning put up with or tolerated something.

clue.text: Sun set to the east by 28, getting dark

indicators.note: 28 is the typist, so each key is swapped for its neighbour immediately to the right on a keyboard

parts.note: taken as written, as three keys on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A typist notes the sun setting in the east as the light fades.
explanation.walkthrough: On a standard QWERTY keyboard the key just right of S is D, right of U is I, and right of N is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim means faint or poorly lit, as a room is when it is getting dark.

clue.text: Key worker making some faulty pistons

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters are a run lying within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An essential mechanic working on defective engine parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' suggests an essential employee; it is someone who works the keys of a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist presses the keys of a typewriter or keyboard all day, a worker of keys.

clue.text: Balance that bid shows

definitions.meaning: first meaning: even proportion between two sides
second meaning: the property the written word bid has, being a mirror image about its middle letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'bid' looks like an offer, but it is the three letters themselves: b and d are mirror images either side of i.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an exact match of two halves of a shape around a central line, a pleasing balance.
